subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — burst cadence, prewarm signals, and headroom for ZenithOps
messages:
From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@zenithops.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@zenithops.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity question — burst cadence and prewarm signals

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we finalize the Reserved Capacity line item I need a clearer picture of how Redwood will handle short, sharp spikes (our nightly data-processing pipelines tend to create 90–120s bursts 2x/day). Specifically: 

- How do you define "burst" vs. normal autoscale in Dedicated? Can we set a per-deal burst budget (credits) so we don't consume baseline throughput?
- What prewarm signal options do you support (predictive CPU/p99 queue, webhook, metrics-based)? How long does a prewarm take for a 16-GPU slab to hit readiness?
- Is there a hard cap on scale-rate (GPUs/min) and a cooldown window? We need to avoid noisy neighbor eviction during these windows.
- How do you bill transient bursts (per-second tokens, or a blended reserved+burst model)?

I've attached a small usage sample (zenith_current_usage.csv) and our current SLA expectations. Can you propose an ops pattern we can include in the SOW that handles: 1) nightly 2-minute bursts, 2) an ad-hoc customer-driven flood (webhook-driven) for up to 10 minutes, and 3) graceful fallback if Dedicated headroom exhausted?

Looking to finalize commercials by end of week. Appreciate a short proposal and an ops cadence (prewarm rules, cooldowns, credits) we can include in procurement paperwork.

Best,
Liam
Operations Lead — ZenithOps

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@zenithops.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@zenithops.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — burst cadence and prewarm signals

Hi Liam — thanks for the usage sample, that helps. High-level proposal below; attached is a short template (dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) we use to lock in headroom and burst credits. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through.

Summary (proposal):
- Mode: Reserved baseline + burst credits 
  - Baseline: reserve slab(s) sized to cover your 95th percentile sustained batch windows (we'll recommend exact slab count after you fill the template).
  - Burst credits: a per-deal bucket of ephemeral GPU-minutes that can be consumed above baseline. Credits reset monthly (or can be one-off for ramp events).

- Prewarm signals supported:
  - Metrics-based predictive prewarm (we watch your job queue p95/p99 and kick prewarm when slope > threshold)
  - Webhook trigger (your pipeline calls a Redwood webhook; we start prewarm immediately)
  - Scheduled prewarm (cron-style) for known nightly jobs

- Latency / time-to-ready:
  - Typical prewarm to readiness for a 16-GPU slab: 45–90s depending on model warming (KV cache behavior). We guarantee <120s for standard image + warm cache; cold-starts can be longer.

- Scale-rate & cooldowns:
  - Default soft max: 4 GPUs/min per reservation pool; can be tuned per-deal.
  - Cooldown: default 3m after a scale-up before we consider an immediate scale-down; this reduces churn and eviction.
  - Eviction policy: fair-share across dedicated pools, prioritized by deal tier + canary fallback to host pooled inference if eviction necessary.

- Billing model:
  - Baseline: monthly reserved fee for slabs.
  - Bursts: consumed from credits at a per-GPU-minute rate; if credits exhausted, bursts billed at on-demand per-minute pricing or automatically fall back to hosted variant depending on policy.

Suggested SOW language (ops cadence):
- We will provision baseline slabs as agreed in dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx.
- ZenithOps receives a monthly burst credit pool of X GPU-minutes (TBD).
- Prewarm policy: Redwood will enable webhook + metrics-based prewarm. Webhook calls are honored within 5s and prewarm cycles prioritized.
- Fallback: if burst credits exhausted and capacity constrained, Redwood will either (a) fail requests with 429 (configurable), (b) route to a hosted-compatible model for non-sensitive traffic, or (c) honor a limited paid overage rate.

Next steps: please fill the attached template (fields: peak concurrency, model sizes, p95 sequence length, expected prewarm lead time) and suggest 30–45 minute slot today or tomorrow. I'll loop in our Platform person for concrete cooldowns.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity question — burst cadence and prewarm signals

Markus / Neha — quick internal note before I join the call:

- For Zenith's pattern (two short nightly spikes + occasional webhook floods) I'd recommend:
  1) Burst credit pool sized for 3x nightly spike (safety) with monthly auto-top-up threshold at 70% consumption.
  2) Max scale-rate = 6 GPUs/min for first 2 minutes only (fast ramp window) then throttle to 2 GPUs/min to limit cluster churn.
  3) Add a soft admission control: if prewarm latency > 90s we return a lightweight queued response with ETA (avoid cascading retries).
  4) Telemetry: emit per-deal prewarm start/ready events to their metrics webhook so they can reconcile.

- Ops playbook snippet we should include in SOW:
  - Prewarm webhook spec (payload + retry semantics).
  - Max burst per-event cap (e.g., 160 GPU-minutes) to avoid single job draining the whole pool.
  - Billing fallback rules (automated on-demand or failover to hosted).

I'll bring suggested knob values to the call (I'll propose numeric GPU-minute values).

- One operational caveat: if Zenith wants low p50 latency during bursts for real-time endpoints we need to prefer prewarm + pinned KV caches rather than pure scale-up — that increases baseline costs. We'll highlight tradeoffs for procurement.

— Priyom
Principal Product Manager, Capacity | Redwood Inference

From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@zenithops.com>

Thanks Markus & team — this is exactly the level of detail procurement needs. A few quick confirmations: 

- We can accept a monthly burst credit pool and a one-off top-up in month 1 for onboarding. Please propose a nominal X (Priyom — if you can suggest the numeric safety multiplier here, that would be great).
- We want the webhook prewarm flow; will send engineering the webhook contract and a sample payload today.
- For fallback, procurement prefers automatic on-demand billing rather than 429s for customer-facing endpoints (we'll absorb cost for a short period). Can you add the billing fallback language into the SOW draft and send us the SLA addendum for signature?

I'll schedule a 30m call tomorrow at 10:00 PT and upload the completed sizing template before the call. Priya will own procurement.

Thanks —
Liam
